findings.summary: AttributesDict freeze mechanism is bypassable via pop(), clear(), and popitem() because those methods do not route through __delitem__ in CPython
findings.failure_scenario: After attributes_dict.freeze() is called, calling attributes_dict.pop('some_key') succeeds silently (removes the key without raising TypeError), because CPython's dict.pop() uses internal C-level deletion that bypasses the Python __delitem__ override. Same applies to .clear() and .popitem(). The frozen invariant is not fully enforced.

findings.summary: Test test_user_cannot_modify_call_weave_dict incorrectly expects mutation of call.attributes to succeed during op execution; attributes are frozen at create_call time before the function body runs
findings.failure_scenario: The test line 'call.attributes["test"] = 123' inside the op function does not wrap in pytest.raises(TypeError), implying mutation is allowed. But attributes_dict.freeze() runs before the function body, so this assignment raises TypeError. The test passes only because _call_sync_func catches the exception and calls finish(exception=TypeError(...)), which records the call as errored — not the intended behavior the test comment ('# allowed in this context') describes. This contradicts test_current_call.py::test_call_attributes_read_only which correctly expects TypeError.
